anomalies.GEN.828: hot Jupiters per M dwarf are about 0.07 to 0.12 against under 0.002 observed
anomalies.GEN.829: planets of 10 to 50 Earth masses outnumber those of 2 to 10: the mass function is inverted against observation

reference.kind: observed rates (recalled by Aux 16, tier T2/T3, unverified)

cold_giants.source: giants at 1 to 10 AU about 0.10 to 0.15 per FGK star (Fulton et al. 2021, 0.3 to 10 AU)

earth_mass_in_hz.source: Earth-mass planets in the ecosphere (eta-Earth) 0.2 to 0.6 per Sun-like star (Bryson et al. 2021, Petigura et al. 2018), widened for 300 stars

giants.source: giants of 100 Earth masses or more about 0.15 to 0.25 per FGK star (Wright et al. 2012, Fulton et al. 2021)

hot_jupiters.source: hot Jupiters about 0.005 to 0.01 per FGK star (Wright et al. 2012; Fressin et al. 2013: 0.0043), widened for 300 stars

inner_planets.source: 1 to 20 Earth-mass planets inside 0.5 AU about 0.5 to 1 per FGK star (Fressin et al. 2013, Zhu et al. 2018, Petigura et al. 2018)

super_earths_per_neptune.source: planets of 2 to 10 Earth masses outnumber those of 10 to 50: the mass function falls steadily above about 10 Earth masses (Fressin et al. 2013, Petigura et al. 2018)

giants.source: giants about 0.03 to 0.06 per M dwarf (Johnson et al. 2010, Bonfils et al. 2013), widened for 100 stars

hot_jupiters.source: hot Jupiters under 0.002 per M dwarf (Johnson et al. 2010; transit surveys), widened for 100 stars
